bull_bear.body: Prioritizing capex for domestic capacity expansion (Haryana) and electrification tech; no dividend or buyback mentioned; royalty payments fully in INR; no equity raise planned; focus on operational efficiency over JV capex sharing
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Semiconductor shortages limiting production (51K units unproduced in Q1); unpredictable commodity prices; regulatory uncertainty around 6-airbag norms (effective Oct 1, 2022); hybrid taxation disadvantage partially offset but still a concern; export market volatility in EMs; supply chain fragility
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, bullish, and proactive; strong emphasis on product-led growth, technology leadership (hybrid), and long-term decarbonization; dismissive of short-term OPEX noise; assertive on market share capture; transparent on constraints (supply chain, costs)
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Grand Vitara is manufactured by Toyota Kirloskar at cost (no profit markup) under exclusive contract, making it a de facto Maruti product for accounting and margin purposes; 45-50% hybrid uptake in Grand Vitara exceeds industry expectations and signals consumer readiness for premium electrification; Haryana plant decision reflects operational logic over corporate accounting — Maruti owns the factory despite Suzuki’s global ownership
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Brezza: 70K bookings, 50%+ in top Zxi+ and Zxi variants; Grand Vitara: 20K bookings, 45-50% strong hybrid (I-EH); CNG: 20% of total sales; Exports: 69,437 units (all-time high); Mid-SUV segment: ~50% of total SUV market (~40% of overall passenger vehicle market)

business.body:
- Sales are split 81.7% Domestic (557,988 units) and 18.3% Exports (124,736 units) of Q1 FY'27 total sales of 682,724 units, with exports growing 28.6% YoY against domestic 29.5%.
- The company also supplies other manufacturers: "Sales to other OEM" of 23,181 units was 4.2% of domestic sales, the only line to decline (-19.5% YoY).
- The deck presents standalone figures only; all figures are in INR million except sales volume and ratios, and "Due to rounding-off, ratios may be approximate".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Amalgamation] "Suzuki Motor Gujarat Private Limited (SMG), a wholly owned subsidiary of Maruti Suzuki India Limited (MSIL), amalgamated with MSIL starting December 1, 2025. Since the appointed date as per the Scheme of amalgamation is April 1, 2025, the financial statements for the relevant periods have been restated for comparison purpose."
- [Non-operating income] Non-operating income at 3.7% of net sales in Q1 FY'27 was well above Q4 FY'26's 1.0% (+270 bps) but below Q1 FY'26's 5.1% (-140 bps); it is large enough that PBT (8.7% of net sales) materially exceeds Op. EBIT (5.1%).
- [Scope] The deck's contents are limited to two period comparisons plus a sales-volume slide — there is no product roadmap, order book, dealer/network data, EV or powertrain commentary, or outlook section.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Commodity inflation impacted margins by ~200 bps in Q1; partially offset by 130 bps price hike; sales promotion cost increased by Rs.1,500/vehicle QoQ; employee cost increase (0.6%) due to salary hikes; gross margin declined 100 bps QoQ; royalty fixed at 3.7% in rupees; yen exposure now ~3% of net sales (direct), ~JPY 85B indirect annual
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: No formal guidance issued; management expects commodity cost pressures to ease in Q2, yen depreciation benefit to materialize in Q2 and beyond, and continued strong demand for Brezza and Grand Vitara to drive volume and margin expansion.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: 350,000 units total; 70,000 for All-New Brezza; 20,000 for Grand Vitara
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion of strong hybrid tech to other models; Haryana plant (250K units/year by 2025); Export market diversification via Suzuki's global network; Potential CNG and EV pipeline beyond current offerings
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Maruti Suzuki is redefining its market leadership by aggressively expanding its high-margin SUV portfolio with cutting-edge hybrid technology, leveraging Toyota's manufacturing partnership to accelerate electrification while navigating persistent semiconductor shortages and commodity inflation through strategic pricing and cost controls.

open.item: Commission two new manufacturing plants in FY 2026-27, one at Kharkhoda (Haryana) and one at Hansalpur (Gujarat), with an annual capacity of 250,000 units each.
The share of cars despatched by rail is expected to reach 28% in FY 2026-27, from 26.5% in FY 2025-26.
Chairman's message: this year's target is 9 lakh CNG cars, after CNG sales rose 22% to 7.46 lakh cars in FY 2025-26.
As a result of the expansion projects, installed capacity is to reach 2.9 million units at the end of FY 2026-27 and 3.65 million units at the end of FY 2030-31.
open.promised: 2.9 million by end FY 2026-27; 3.65 million by end FY 2030-31 units

open.item: The Company expects to sustain export volumes at FY 2025-26 levels despite continuing geopolitical uncertainties.
Volume growth of around 10% is expected in FY 2026-27, enabled by the 500,000 units of manufacturing capacity added in FY 2026-27.
Carbon footprint in the production process is to reduce from the present 615,000 tonnes to 266,000 tonnes in FY 2030-31.

Chairman's estimate of the market the Company plans against: the car industry would grow to 6.1 to 6.3 million units by FY 2030-31, with the small car market growing significantly faster than in the last five years - an estimate that could lead to changes in the Company's longer-term targets.
Water intensity in the production process is expected to decrease by 17% by FY 2030-31 compared with FY 2025-26.
By FY 2030-31 the Company intends to use over 20 tonnes of biogas per day.
Solar energy use is to rise from 79 MWp at the end of FY 2025-26 to 319 MWp by 2030-31, with 214 MWp generated in-house.
Renewable electricity is to increase from the present 23% to 85% by FY 2030-31.
Introduce 7 SUVs in the next 5 years to further strengthen the SUV portfolio.
Scale production capacity to four million units per annum over the next few years (MD&A); the risk section dates this ambition to FY 2030-31.
Install a railway siding at Kharkhoda similar to the one operating at the Manesar plant.

Start four biogas plants in the first phase at a cost of INR 561 crores, as approved by the Board, with an intent to invest substantially more in biogas production and distribution once the process and technology are proven.

risks.note: The Company aims to scale production to four million units annually by FY 2030-31, nearly double its current capacity. It took almost 40 years to reach two million units; the next two million is to be added in just 7-8 years, a pace nearly five times faster. This requires significantly more human capital, financial investment and technical know-how plus faster decision-making, and stakeholder partners - suppliers, dealers and transporters - must scale in tandem.
risks.risk: Risks associated with the increased scale of operations

risks.note: With nearly 450 Tier-1 and about 1,500 Tier-2 suppliers, supply disruption remains a major business continuity risk. Export restrictions on certain critical materials during the year highlighted the vulnerability of globally concentrated supply chains, and geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions and logistics disruptions may continue to affect supply availability. Mitigation is localisation, alternate sources, diversified sourcing locations and the Vendor Comprehensive Excellence Programme.
risks.risk: Continuity of component supplies across a concentrated supplier base

risks.note: Increasing adoption of advanced automotive technologies raises dependence on specialised materials and critical components whose supply chains remain concentrated in a few countries; in an increasingly dynamic geopolitical environment, material-availability risk is likely to persist. In the near term, geopolitical tensions in West Asia may exert pressure on profitability through higher commodity prices.
risks.risk: Dependence on specialised materials and critical components sourced from a limited number of countries

risks.note: Electrification, software-defined vehicles, advanced electronics and connectivity are transforming the industry, but several of these technologies are yet to reach the cost competitiveness needed for widespread adoption in a price-sensitive market such as India. As the BEV, SHEV and advanced-feature portfolio expands, holding cost competitiveness while preserving affordability is a key strategic priority, addressed through localisation, value engineering and supplier base expansion.
risks.risk: Cost competitiveness of emerging and advanced technologies in a price-sensitive market

risks.note: Sudden and significant increases in the prices of metals, energy and other commodities can adversely impact profitability and business performance, a risk reinforced by recent geopolitical developments. This risk materialised in FY 2025-26: operating margin moderated to 8.4% from 10.0%, driven by adverse commodity prices and supply-side pressures, with the Company choosing not to pass on the full cost increases. Mitigation includes consumption optimisation, alternate materials, material circularity, hedging, forward contracts and long-term commercial arrangements.

Scaling operations amid rapid technological transformation increases demand for new skillsets both internally and across value chain partners; at the same time, sustaining the organisational values, culture of partnership and continuous-improvement spirit built over four decades becomes harder as scale and workforce expand.
risks.risk: Capacity and capability for future readiness - skills, leadership pipeline and cultural continuity at scale

risks.note: Cyber threats are growing and the Company protects information assets through employee education on phishing and proactive monitoring. It has created a cybersecurity assessment framework based on global standards for suppliers, and over 400 Tier-1 supplier partners have been assessed so far, on the view that supply-chain cyber resilience is a business-continuity issue.
risks.risk: Cybersecurity, including cyber risk in the supply chain

risks.note: The Company is exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates, mainly on the import of components, raw materials and services and on the export of vehicles and services. It runs a structured exchange risk management policy and uses hedge instruments judiciously depending on market conditions and the currency view. The MD&A separately records a sharp depreciation of the rupee against the US dollar towards the end of the year.
risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure on imports and exports
